title: Global Sales of Professional Service Robots Surge 24%
source_used: International Federation of Robotics (IFR), its World Robotics 2026 Service Robots press release
key_facts: Global shipments of professional service robots rose 24% to almost 250,000 units in 2025.
Transport and logistics was the top use, with 117,500 units sold (up 21%, a 47% share); hospitality robots came second and professional cleaning robots third.
Consumer service robots rose 37% to almost 34.2 million units, and surgical robots rose 57% to 8,400 units.
About 7,000 full-size humanoid robots (above 140 cm) were sold globally in 2025.
Most current humanoid applications are specialized and often require human teleoperation.
Safety standards, high training and maintenance costs, and a weak business case still limit adoption.
quote_evidence: Global shipments of professional service robots increased by 24% to almost 250,000 units in 2025, highlighting a successful shift to commercial automation.
In 2025, about 7,000 units of full-size humanoids (above 140 cm) were sold globally.
why_it_matters_hint: Robots are moving from pilots into everyday work in logistics, hotels and cleaning.
notes: The federation's own release; the figures are its own. The release points to a separate position paper on service robots, not read.
